think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 16-year-old male with recreational gardening and drug exposures presents with acute/subacute B-symptoms (daily fevers, drenching sweats, profound 10-kg weight loss), generalized painful lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and massive chylous ascites. This presentation closely mimics aggressive hematologic malignancies (such as Hodgkin or non-Hodgkin lymphoma), disseminated histoplasmosis, or abdominal tuberculosis. The diagnostic challenge is recognizing the juvenile form of a systemic endemic mycosis presenting with lymphatic obstruction and chyloperitoneum without disclosing tissue histology.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Day 1 admission triage concludes after physical examination, admission imaging (CT showing generalized supradiaphragmatic and infradiaphragmatic lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, large ascites), baseline blood work (CBC showing anemia, leukocytosis with left shift and marked eosinophilia; elevated ALP, GGT, CRP), and paracentesis confirming chylous ascites by lipid profile. Confirmatory testing begins with surgical excisional biopsy of an inguinal lymph node and counterimmunoelectrophoresis serology.
3. Differential Distinctions: Lymphoma is ruled out by lymph node biopsy demonstrating non-caseating/suppurative granulomas containing multi-budding yeasts rather than clonal neoplastic cells. Disseminated histoplasmosis is excluded by serologic counterimmunoelectrophoresis (barely 1:1 for Histoplasma vs 1:512 for Paracoccidioides) and fungal morphology showing large yeasts with multiple circumferential buds (mariner's wheel) rather than small uniform intracellular yeasts.
case_prompt:
A 16-year-old previously healthy adolescent male residing in the urban area of São Paulo state, Brazil, is admitted to the hospital with a 3-week history of generalized lymphadenopathy. His history includes tobacco use (5-6 cigarettes daily), recreational marijuana and cocaine use, and frequent gardening.

He reports daily vespertine fevers accompanied by profound fatigue, prostration, drenching diaphoresis, and an unintentional 10-kg weight loss over 3 weeks. In addition, he reports ventilatory-dependent right hemithoracic chest pain and lower esophageal dysphagia with solid food intake.

On physical examination, he appears chronically ill. Multiple lymph nodes measuring 1 to 3 cm are palpable throughout all superficial cervical, axillary, and inguinal chains; the nodes are mobile and tender. Abdominal examination reveals hepatomegaly, with the liver edge palpable 4 cm below the right costal margin, as well as abdominal distension with shifting dullness.

Initial laboratory testing reveals normocytic normochromic anemia, leukocytosis with neutrophilia and a left shift, intense peripheral eosinophilia, and elevated serum alkaline phosphatase, gamma-glutamyl transferase, and C-reactive protein levels. Admission imaging demonstrates extensive mesenteric, retroperitoneal, pelvic, inguinal, mediastinal, and hilar lymphadenopathy, marked hepatosplenomegaly, and large-volume ascites. Paracentesis demonstrates milky fluid consistent with chylous ascites by lipid comparison with serum.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Strongly suspected given the acute B-symptoms (fever, drenching sweats, 10-kg weight loss), diffuse generalized lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and massive chylous ascites in an adolescent, but excluded by lymph node histopathology demonstrating granulomatous fungal inflammation with multiple exosporulations rather than malignant lymphoid proliferation.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Imaging tests performed during hospital admission revealed mesenteric, retroperitoneal, pelvic, inguinal, mediastinal, and hilar lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and large-volume ascites (Figure 1).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the reticuloendothelial involvement, fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and South American geographic origin, but ruled out by specific serologic counterimmunoelectrophoresis showing only a 1:1 titer against Histoplasma capsulatum compared to a diagnostic 1:512 titer against Paracoccidioides, as well as distinct fungal morphology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Additionally, in the counterimmunoelectrophoresis test, anti-Paracoccidioides spp. and anti-Histoplasma capsulatum serum antibodies had titers of 1:512 and 1:1, respectively.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Confirmed by excisional inguinal lymph node biopsy revealing epithelioid granulomas with multinucleated giant cells and characteristic fungal yeast structures with multiple exosporulations (mariner's wheel appearance) consistent with Paracoccidioides spp., supported by counterimmunoelectrophoresis titers of 1:512.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: An inguinal lymph node biopsy revealed granuloma formation with epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated giant cells, numerous circular and oval fungal structures considerably varying in size, and some with multiple exosporulations inside and outside granulomas, suggesting Paracoccidioides spp. (Figure 2).

editor_comments: Admission breakpoint strictly respected. All biopsy, serology, and antifungal treatment details excluded from case prompt. Exact quotes verified from article text.
